title: Construction Equipment Accounting
description: Complete guide to equipment accounting including capitalization, depreciation, internal rental rates, equipment cost allocation, lease accounting, and equipment management systems.

sections.title: Equipment Capitalization and Depreciation
sections.content:
Construction equipment represents a significant capital investment for contractors, often comprising 20-40% of total assets. Proper accounting for equipment acquisition, depreciation, and cost allocation is essential for accurate job costing and financial reporting.

## Capitalization Criteria

Equipment is capitalized when:
- Cost exceeds company capitalization threshold (typically $2,500-$5,000)
- Useful life exceeds one year
- Item provides future economic benefit
- Cost includes: purchase price, sales tax, delivery, setup, initial modifications

Expensed immediately:
- Small tools under capitalization threshold
- Repair and maintenance
- Fuel and operating supplies

## Depreciation Methods

### Straight-Line Depreciation
Most common for financial reporting:
```
Annual Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage Value) ÷ Useful Life in Years
```

Example:
- Excavator cost: $350,000
- Salvage value: $70,000 (20%)
- Useful life: 7 years
- Annual depreciation: ($350,000 - $70,000) ÷ 7 = $40,000/year

### Units of Production (Hours-Based)
Preferred for construction equipment as it matches usage:
```
Depreciation per Hour = (Cost - Salvage Value) ÷ Estimated Total Hours
```

Example:
- Same excavator
- Estimated total hours: 10,000 hours
- Depreciation per hour: ($350,000 - $70,000) ÷ 10,000 = $28/hour
- Year 1 usage: 1,200 hours
- Year 1 depreciation: 1,200 × $28 = $33,600

### MACRS (Tax Depreciation)
Most construction equipment is 5-year or 7-year property:
- Light trucks, trailers: 5-year
- Heavy equipment (excavators, dozers, cranes): 5-year
- Office equipment: 5-year or 7-year

**Section 179 Expensing:**
Immediate deduction of up to $1,160,000 (2023 limit) for qualified equipment purchases.

**Bonus Depreciation:**
100% first-year bonus depreciation available for new equipment (phasing down in future years).
